body.x: LiBEST (CEO Kim Joo-Seong) participated in ‘CES 2023’, held in Las Vegas, USA for 4 days between January 5th (Thurs) and 8th (Sun, local time).
LiBEST, a flexible secondary battery manufacturing startup, won the Innovation Award at CES 2023 for their flame retardant and cold resistant battery manufacturing technology.

The fact that the performance of batteries diminishes when temperatures are below 0 degrees (Celsius), like it is these days, is widely known. This has a big effect on the usage time of smartphones and also on the driving distance of EVs. An official of LiBEST explained that, “If temperatures drop even further, you may even experience inoperability. This may lead you to think the product is broken, but it’s normally a battery issue. When temperatures drop, the electrolytes freeze, and this leads to decreased conductivity of lithium ions. This is the reason why lithium-ion batteries normally can only operate at 40~70% of their normal capacity in sub-zero temperatures.”

The flame retardant and cold resistant battery manufacturing technology proposed by LiBEST is unique. The NMC and graphite was used as they were for the anode and cathode, but they combined LiBEST’s special electrolyte and separator film. As such, it has the strengths of maintaining the voltage and high energy density of batteries while gaining the characteristics of flame retardancy and cold resistance.

In regular batteries, when the electrolytes in batteries are directly exposed to flames of around 1,300˚C, regular electrolytes quickly catch fire, and the fire is sustained until all of the electrolytes are burned up. An official of the company explained that, even in the same situation, LiBEST’s electrolytes take much longer to catch fire, like other flame retardant materials, and has the characteristic of being easily extinguishable even when it catches fire, preventing direct combustion at the battery cell level.

Thus, even if there are fires in individual battery cells, it prevents the fire from spreading to the battery pack or the whole, and even if there is a fire in the battery from an accident with the EV, it prevents the fires from spreading to the whole car and even prevents explosions from occurring.

In addition to such flame-retardant properties, it also has cold resistance properties. The electrolyte in the battery that LiBEST is currently developing is able to operate at -40˚C, a temperature that it is impossible for other batteries to operate in, and was shown to charge and discharge normally even in temperatures between –10˚C and –20˚C. In addition, despite being a battery for BEV (battery electric vehicle) with high energy density, it showed a retention capacity of over 90% even after 500 phases of charging and discharging.

An official revealed that, “If you just look at the traits, it appears to be far from commercialization. However, the technical maturity is at the level of TRL 6 and is actually not that far off. Unlike solid-state batteries, which are still slow to commercialize, our batteries can be manufactured using conventional manufacturing processes. As such, it can go into mass production much faster than solid-state batteries and be applied in our lives in general.”

Its range of application is wide too. It can be applied on the flexible batteries, which are one of LiBEST’s main products, to be used to strengthen the safety of VR/AR and metaverse devices or healthcare and medical devices. The smaller batteries with a capacity of 1~5Ah can be applied to delivery robots or drones which are used outdoors and can be derived into a battery system for use in military or special environments as well. It can also be easily applied into pouch or cylindrical types and is expected to be able to be used in urban air mobility (UAM), electric vehicles (EV), or energy storage systems (ESS) when made as a medium-sized or large batteries.
This product was displayed in the LiBEST’s booth for CES at the Las Vegas Convention Center’s Central Hall as well as the Innovation Awards Showcase at The Venetian.

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The Seoul Technology Pavilion operated a Theme Zone which implemented elements of visions for the future and elements for experiences, as well as a Tech Zone which displayed the innovative technology of partnered large corporations and startups. The Seoul Business Agency (SBA) showcased the Seoul Technology Pavilion’s innovative technology in the field of ‘mobility and ESG’ in a large corporation connected open innovation method, and 7 startups possessing innovative technology in the relevant fields will be in participation.
